title: AI Food and Drink Videos With a Fresh Pour | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one bottle or can photo into a vertical pour video with ice and fizz. Use 9:16 for TikTok and Reels with 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds.
h1: Make AI Food and Drink Videos From a Bottle Photo
lead: A static bottle or can cannot show the pour, fizz or first sip. Turn one package photo into a vertical food and drink video with a clear serving moment for TikTok and Reels.
benefits_h2: Why make AI food and drink videos?

benefits.d: Turn one package photo into a pour, first sip or simple preparation so shoppers see how the drink is enjoyed.
Use a vertical 9:16 video paced around one action for TikTok, Instagram Reels and product pages.
Use 6 seconds for one pour, 10 or 15 seconds for a tasting beat, or 30 seconds for a fuller serving story.

benefits.t: Use it in your own ads
benefits.d: Download clips without an AIVideosUGC watermark and add approved flavor, price and allergen details in your editor.

steps_h2: How to Make AI Food and Drink Videos in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn one bottle or can photo into a ready-to-post AI food and drink video.

steps.d: Show the full bottle or can with its shape, cap and drink color visible.
Name the glass, garnish and one serving action, then choose the length and size.
Check the package, then add flavor, price and allergen details before publishing.

faq.q: What source photo works for a drink clip?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo of the full bottle or can with its shape, cap and visible label area clear.

faq.q: Can the video show a pour?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a serving scene with a glass, ice or garnish and keep the package visible beside the action.

faq.q: Can the clip show ice and condensation?
faq.a: Yes. A cold drink scene can include ice, bubbles or condensation. Keep claims about flavor and ingredients in your product listing.

faq.q: What length fits a pour clip?
faq.a: Use 6 seconds for one pour or opening, 10 or 15 seconds for a tasting beat, and 30 seconds for several serving moments.

faq.q: Where do flavor and allergen details go?
faq.a: Add the approved flavor, ingredients and allergen information as text in your editor or product listing after download.

faq.q: Do I need a studio or a creator?
faq.a: No. The clip is generated from your bottle or can photo, so you can prepare a serving scene without booking a kitchen shoot.

visual.overview: An AI food and drink video keeps the package recognizable while a pour, first sip or simple preparation gives viewers one clear serving moment.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and preserve its shape, color and visible label area exactly. A hand pours citrus soda from the silver can into one ice-filled tumbler. Frame at counter height, then make a slow push-in as the glass fills. Bright window light stays visible beside the can. End with the can and full tumbler in frame. Sound: crisp fizz and a soft pour. No music.
